text:
maya: quick check — after the canary push i noticed some debug lines that include `auth_header` field. can someone confirm if tokens are ever sent to our logs?
sam: which canary? can you paste the raw line (sanitise if needed) so i can grep locally?
maya: pasted below, masked the token but you can see the pattern:
```
2026-07-12T08:12:34Z canary-worker DEBUG request_id=abc123 user=svc-canary auth_header=Bearer [UNMASKED_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER] path=/v1/predict
```
jake: thanks — on it. i'll grep the compressed logs in s3 and the streaming raw-logs index.
jake: run: `zgrep -h "auth_header=" /var/log/canary/*.gz | wc -l` -> found 12 matches in last 24h
jake: sample output (sanitised):
```
... auth_header=[MASKED] ...
... auth_header=[MASKED] ...
```
olivia: how are they getting masked? is masking happening at the app or log-forwarder?
sam: masking should happen at the service layer via `redact-headers` middleware before emitting to stdout. looks like canary binary is on an older image maybe without middleware.
maya: can confirm canary was using image redwood/canary:staging-20260711 (older).
security-oncall: immediate ask: are any of those 12 matches showing unmasked token strings (non-[MASKED])?
jake: scanned content of the 12 lines — 11 are `[MASKED]`, 1 had a literal token substring in the stdout before the middleware processed it (it made it into the raw collector buffer).
security-oncall: ok — scope = 1 line possibly containing a real token. what's the retention / exposure surface for that one line?
jake: the raw collector buffer holds ~1MB and is immediately forwarded to s3 bucket `redwood-raw-collector-<region>`. forwarding succeeded. object ACL check next.
olivia: run `aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-raw-collector-us-east-1` -> Owner full control, no public grants.
sam: and bucket policy? `aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-raw-collector-us-east-1` -> restricted to account principals + log-ingest role.
security-oncall: good, so access limited to internal roles. we still treat exposed token as sensitive. immediate mitigations: 1) rotate the token used by the canary job, 2) redact the offending object from s3 and replace with redacted version, 3) patch canary image to include middleware and redeploy.
maya: i'm rotating creds now and will mark the canary job creds as compromised. will post rotation timestamp.
maya: creds rotated at 2026-07-12T08:35:10Z, old token deactivated.
jake: i deleted the raw object from the bucket and replaced with a redacted copy (log line replaced with `auth_header=[MASKED]`). iam change id: ch-20260712-01.
security-oncall: please file an incident entry for tracking — minimal severity but needs comms approval.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2347 — "canary stdout leaked auth_header in raw collector" (severity: low), created by maya at 2026-07-12T08:40:02Z
olivia: minimal severity ok. legal — can you review a short comms blurb? pinging @legal.
legal: thanks olivia — i'll take a look. please send exact scope and remediation steps.
maya: scope: single raw log object uploaded to internal s3; token included in one line. exposure limited to internal IAM principals. remediation: credential rotation, deletion + redacted re-upload, canary image pinned to patched build, add log-forwarder drop rule for `auth_header` before buffer flush.
legal: that reads fine; no customer data found, recommend no external customer notification. internal stakeholders only.
sam: PR to patch image and add CI test for header redaction: https://git.internal/r/redwood/canary/pulls/118
maya: rolling patched canary now to staging, will promote to prod after green smoke tests.
security-oncall: after rotation and delete, is there any remaining access path to the old token (logs elsewhere, backups, index snapshots)?
jake: ran snapshot check — no snapshots contain the token. verified indexes and cloudwatch logs show masked values.
olivia: ok — final ask: legal ok with no external comms, security approves internal postmortem and a 24h follow-up to confirm no further finds.
security-oncall: approving internal comms: short note to #incidents + ops-announce. i'll approve the follow-up checklist.
maya: thanks all — i'll draft the internal blurb and link PR + incident record.
olivia: small action item: add a unit test that ensures middleware redacts headers for future images.
sam: acked and added to backlog (priority P1).
maya: closing notes: root cause = out-of-date canary image without redact middleware; impact = single token line; mitigations complete (rotation + delete + patch); owners = canary eng team + infra.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-2347 updated: status=mitigated, updated_by=maya at 2026-07-12T09:04:48Z
security-oncall: thanks team — keep the incident open until follow-up confirmed in 24h. :thumbsup:
